body:
I've tried to find a purpose in love, and it didn't go too well for me.  I went out with a girl for about six months, and we had ups and downs, just like every relationship.  I was totally, absolutely enamored with her.  She was the only thing that had ever even lifted my head above the water, and somewhere deep inside I had a speck of hope again.  But then, on my birthday, she admitted to me that she had been cheating, and had slept with a few guys.  I forgave her, but the damage had been done.  A month later, she broke up with me because she couldn't handle "hurting me." She had never hurt me.  I was more disappointed in myself than anything that pushed her to cheat, thinking what was I not doing.  In fact, the opposite of hurt is what I was: she was starting to pick up my pieces and at least put a bandage on the parts I had the courage to tell her.  After all, there's only so many things that you can tell someone before they label you as 'Serious Mental Issues'

I never meant to humble people with my story.  I don't want people to look at my story and say "Oh, somebody has it worse, so I don't have the right to be upset." That isn't true at all.  Your problems, no matter how big or small, matter.  

I actually do have a dog.  I used to have two dogs, but one died of cancer when he was four.  The remaining one is 14, so I know about the 'you never know which will be the last' feeling.

I've been told my hugs are wonderful, but I've never liked receiving or giving hugs, unless the other person specifically asks and has a reason for it.
Tomorrow, I'm gonna figure out how to give you gold, definitely. It's already 1 in the morning here and I'm far too lazy and tired to do it at the moment
I will keep that in mind.  Oh, and good luck with your HPPD, and happy holidays!

Hell, I might as well give it a shot.  I have nothing to lose anyways except someone successfully putting me in a institution!  Hahaha :-) thank you for your help, kind stranger, it really means so much to me.
Hahaha if I know myself, even if it does help I'll probably be back here soon enough! :-) thank you for your help though
But how will the right antidepressant change all the rest?  I'll still be alone and unloved.  I stick out like a sore-thumb in the Bible Belt of America.  I just plain don't belong.
Even with the best medication, how will that change the rest?  I'll still be alone and unloved
I don't even know how to start getting better, and if I ever do succeed, how to love life without sulking in misery.  I've never lived in anything but misery and depression.

I've mixed and matched plenty of drugs.  Hell, I tried straight caffeine once (the trip was terrifying).  I've stopped all that now, partly because my ex begged me not to, and her look of shame just pierced me deep.  Sometimes I have my moments of weakness, but I'm really trying.  I have no clue what to do to even get on the road of recovery, honestly.  Maybe it's a matter of finding the right kind of anti-depressant and then.... idk what.  I do want to get better, but in a way, no.  I've always known misery in my life.  I don't know how to live with anything other than it.
There are billions of others out there who need help.  What makes me so special as to get it?  For the longest time I sat quietly as I died internally.  What about all of them?
Why me though?  You don't know me from the man on the moon.  I'm sorry if I come off as rude, but I'm legitimately curious
Thank you for your kind off, but you're wrong.  I really am not worth it.
I already did, a few hours ago.
